entries.claim: The regression test does not actually guarantee that workflows contain no secret reads or signing steps; it only rejects four exact, case-sensitive substrings.
entries.failure_scenario: A workflow can sign artifacts with a command such as `gpg --detach-sign artifact`, `cosign sign artifact`, or `openssl dgst -sign key.pem artifact`, and this test passes because none contains `-Y sign`. Likewise, alternate expression formatting or an action that accepts a secret-backed signing key can evade these literals. The asserted policy that CI never signs or reads release secrets can therefore regress without failing the test.

counter_evidence.note: True that the test matches literals and a workflow could read secrets through toJSON(secrets) or sign with gpg or cosign without tripping it. But D-11 fixes this exact list as a regression tripwire, and the guarantee itself rests on the repository holding 0 Actions secrets and 0 environments (gh api, 2026-10-14; PLAN-2 Task 4 verify re-reads it), so a workflow has no secret to read and CI holds no key to sign with. Low, not fixed.
